speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms of double vision and muscle weakness? Also, do you notice that these symptoms worsen later in the day or with activity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids? Also, do you have any history of thyroid disease or other autoimmune conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the weakness is symmetrical and there is no family history of neurological disease. To help narrow this down, I need to know: do you have difficulty swallowing or speaking, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying those details. I would like to examine your eyelids directly for ptosis and check your reflexes. I will also request an Acetylcholine receptor antibody test and a Chest CT to rule out a thymoma. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT
